key: And the LORD smote the king, so that he was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a house set apart. And Jotham the king’s son was over the household, judging the people of the land.
s: Opening a chapter of conspiracies in Israel, Judah’s Azariah does right yet is stricken; Metzudat David, on 15:5, reads the ‘house set apart’ as release from the toil of governing, kingship counting, as the sages say, as servitude, and Rashi, on 15:5, as a house he made himself among the graves.
src: Metzudat David and Rashi on 2 Kings 15:5, Hebrew (On Your Way; the Metsudah Tanach series) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

evidence.words: בבית החפשית. רצה לומר: עזב הנהגת המלכות, והיה חפשי מזה העמל, וכמו שאמרו רבותינו ז״ל שהמלכות יחשב לעבדות, לפי רוב העמל … בְּבֵית הַחָפְשִׁית. עָשָׂה לוֹ בַּיִת בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת, כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אֲמַר בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי
evidence.gloss: Metzudat David: “In the house of freedom”: that is, he left the governing of the kingdom and was free of that toil, as our rabbis said that kingship is reckoned servitude, for the greatness of its toil. Rashi: “In the house of freedom”: he made himself a house in the cemetery, as it is said, “free among the dead”.
